data.body:
**[P2] Ensure every drain covers records pending when it starts**

When a flush is already queued or in flight, this logic can treat it as sufficient even if its barrier predates a newly pending record. A recordless drain may then return when that older flush completes; the worker exports the record afterward without another flush, leaving buffered telemetry vulnerable to Lambda freeze. Snapshot the global schedule sequence at drain entry, widen any queued barrier to that sequence, and track in-flight sequence coverage so only a flush covering that snapshot is shared. Add both queued-flush and in-flight-flush ordering tests.
